### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6b44efa7b4a429994dc6d92c3de96392d4e03f3f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7316682282de9ecdd7b57175b107d64edb48641d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/internal-field-readback.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/internal-field-readback.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-domain-verification-instructed-record.test.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/register-sso-provider.ts (`dnsRecordValue`, `runVerifyDomain`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/objectql-adapter.ts (`findOne` / `findMany` / `consumeOne` and the seam calls), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts (the `sso()` options and the adapter construction), packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-verification.object.ts (the `internal` declaration), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`omitInternalFields`, `resolveInternalField`), content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx, `@better-auth/sso` 1.7.12 `dist/index.mjs` (`verifyDomain`, `requestDomainVerification`, `getVerificationIdentifier`, `checkProviderAccess`, `parseProviderDomains`), `better-auth` 1.7.12 `dist/db/internal-adapter.mjs` (`findVerificationValue`, `consumeVerificationValue`). The changeset `.changeset/25111-sso-domain-verification-instructed-record.md` is read as a prose face: its level and declaration lines only, under ②.

Inputs: card #25111 (body and both comments: the dispatch claim and the os-dev-report), PR #25161 (body, file list, and the net diff against `main` at merge base `23540582f`: 4 files, +409/-10), and the check-runs on the head. Vendor code was read from the published npm tarballs of `@better-auth/sso`, `better-auth`, `@better-auth/oauth-provider` and `@better-auth/scim` at 1.7.12 (the versions `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/package.json` pins), extracted into scratch and never executed. Nothing was built, run or re-run locally.

Check-runs on the head, read at 2026-10-22T03:16Z: 40 runs; 28 completed `success`, 7 completed `skipped` (the opt-in and path-filtered lanes: Temporal Conformance, the Dogfood Regression Gate shards, Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Verify CLI, Build Docs, Packed-tarball smoke, 18.x upgrade harness), and 5 still `in_progress`: Test Core 1/6, 2/6, 3/6, 4/6 and 6/6. Green among the completed: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, every Lint lane, Type Check workspace / consumer gates / source gates / debt ledger, Build Core, Test Core 5/6, and the five PM claim guards. The in-progress shards were not waited for; their conclusions stay the gate verdicts for the queue.

### ① Derived judgments

The diff changes one thing at runtime: `READBACK_FIELDS[sys_verification]` in `internal-field-readback.ts` gains `{ field: 'identifier', absenceProvesStrip: true }` beside `value`. Everything below follows from that one row.

**(a) What the seam feeds, and whether any caller outside the vendor now reads wider.** Right: it widens only what the vendor's storage adapter sees. `reattachInternalFieldsOnRead` is imported by exactly one module, `objectql-adapter.ts`, and called at three verbs: `findOne` (:955, with the read's own `where` as the lookup), `findMany` (:1010, no lookup), `consumeOne` (:1154, no lookup). That adapter is constructed in one place, `auth-manager.ts:4777`, as the `database` factory better-auth is handed; no other module imports `createObjectQLAdapterFactory`, and no non-test module in plugin-auth names `sys_verification` or `SystemObjectName.VERIFICATION` outside the seam and the manifest, so no plugin-auth route, service or export holds the adapter or reads the table through it. Every other exit reaches the row through the engine's generic read path, where `omitInternalFields` (engine.ts:11534, run from `maskSecretFields` on every `find` / `findOne`) deletes every `internal: true` column with no `isSystem` carve-out: the data door (`sys_verification` is `apiMethods: ['get']`, `access: private`, `defaultRowScope` `id == null`), MCP and export reads over the engine, and the compliance ledger's CRUD mirror that honours the same flag. `resolveInternalField` (engine.ts:11816) is a separately named privileged verb off the RAW engine, unreachable from a query string, and refuses any column not flagged `internal`. The PR's precondition case pins the generic `engine.find` under `isSystem: true` still omitting `identifier` after the change, while storage holds it.

Inside the vendor, the hunk's "only reader" claim was re-traced on the four 1.7.12 dists rather than taken from the comment. Every `.identifier` read off a verification row: `@better-auth/sso` `verifyDomain` (index.mjs:2639) is the one; better-auth core reads `data.identifier` only on the create input (internal-adapter.mjs:717, :902); core's `test-utils` plugin reads it off a row in a test helper, and plugin-auth mounts no such plugin; oauth-provider's `.identifier` hits are its resource model and path params, not verification rows; scim has none. No route echoes a verification row to its caller: across the 37 `findVerificationValue` / `consumeVerificationValue` call sites in the four dists, no receiving variable is passed to `ctx.json(` whole or spread (a static census; the `.identifier` census above is the stronger one for this column). The value the vendor is now handed is one it computed itself (`getVerificationIdentifier`, index.mjs:2544) and passed in as the lookup key.

**(b) Is the newly accepted record exactly the one the platform instructs?** Right. `register-sso-provider.ts:485-488` answers `dnsRecordName` = `_better-auth-token-PROVIDER.DOMAIN` and `dnsRecordValue` = `_better-auth-token-PROVIDER=TOKEN`, the token being the vendor's `domainVerificationToken`; `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx:260-262` tells the operator to publish exactly those two fields. The vendor queries TXT at `IDENTIFIER.DOMAIN` with `IDENTIFIER` = `_` + (`tokenPrefix` or `better-auth-token`) + `-` + `provider.providerId` (index.mjs:2544, :2606, :2634) and accepts a trimmed record equal to `row.identifier + '=' + row.value` or to `row.value` alone (index.mjs:2638-2642). plugin-auth passes `sso({ domainVerification: { enabled: true } })` with no `tokenPrefix` and no `verification.storeIdentifier` anywhere in its source (auth-manager.ts:4529-4531), so the stored identifier is the plain computed label, identical to the bridge's `SSO_DOMAIN_TOKEN_PREFIX` spelling. With the row whole, the vendor's `IDENTIFIER=VALUE` form is byte for byte the instructed `dnsRecordValue`. Before the fix, the platform's published text already contradicted its own verify door, which is the shape the card and the dispatch describe.

**(c) Is the newly refused `undefined=TOKEN` record producible by anything but the defect?** Right: it is not. The identifier is `_` + prefix + `-` + providerId, so it always starts with `_` and can never spell `undefined`. The string arose only from the template literal over a row the strip had emptied, and only on an engine that strips (the ObjectQL engine); on a non-stripping adapter the vendor never accepted it. No instruction, doc, test or UI ever named it. Removing it removes a defect artefact, not a published member of the accept set.

**(d) Does the verification still prove control of the DNS name for that provider?** Right. The vendor never reads the DNS name from the row: it queries `IDENTIFIER.domain` for every domain in `parseProviderDomains(provider.domain)` (index.mjs:139, :2632-2634) with the identifier computed from the stored provider id, and the token is a fresh 24-character random value stored under that identifier (`requestDomainVerification`, index.mjs:2573-2578; `registerSSOProvider`, :3539). A wrong token, another provider's label inside the value, and the instructed value published at another provider's name are each refused 502 `DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_FAILED` and leave `domain_verified` false; the new suite pins all three on both doors with the queried DNS name asserted. The label inside the value repeats what the queried name already binds, so the bare-token form the vendor accepts by design is neither weaker nor changed. The dispatch's premise that remedy B would make the published record prove less does not hold against the vendor code, and the dev was right not to raise it as needs_decision.

**Full accept-set delta of the verify door**, vendor route and bridge alike: `_better-auth-token-PROVIDER=TOKEN` goes from refused 502 to accepted (204 vendor / 200 bridge, `verified: true`); `undefined=TOKEN` goes from accepted to refused 502 `DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_FAILED`; bare `TOKEN`, wrong token, wrong label and wrong name are unchanged. A provider already verified stays verified (`domain_verified` persists; a later verify answers 409 `DOMAIN_VERIFIED`), so no verified tenant is touched. No request field, response field, route, error code or object declaration changes; `register-sso-provider.ts` and `sys-verification.object.ts` are untouched by the diff.

**Consistency of the new seam row.** `identifier` is `required: true` (`sys-verification.object.ts:136-139`), so `absenceProvesStrip: true` is the correct posture, the same one `value` already carries on this table: a stripping engine without the accessor already threw for `value`, so no new failure class is introduced, and on a non-stripping engine the rows carry the column and the seam is a no-op. The three seam pins cover both columns on the `findMany` shape, the lookup answer on a read keyed on `identifier`, and the fail-closed throw. The fail-closed consequence text now names domain verification, which matches the measured consequence.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no`, bare, is right; it must not read `no (narrowing)`. The repo's rule (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, the arm's provenance) is that the `(narrowing)` arm declares a PUBLISHED accept set shrank, which is breaking. The only record this diff stops accepting is `undefined=TOKEN`, which (c) shows no published text ever named and nothing but the defect could produce; the published accept set, the record `request-domain-verification` answers plus the vendor's bare-token form, is not narrowed but honoured for the first time. The widening side is the removal of a refusal the platform's own contract text already contradicted (`dnsRecordValue` in `register-sso-provider.ts` and `sso.mdx`), and both declaration lines cite that text: the PR body's line names "the record the platform already tells the operator to publish" with the file and function in the section under it, and the changeset's line names "the record the platform already names" with the route in its body. That is the `no` case, not `yes`. With no `(narrowing)` arm and no `!` in the title, the full dogfood battery is not owed; the dev's `dogfood_battery: n/a` reading is right.

Changeset level: `.changeset/25111-sso-domain-verification-instructed-record.md` grades `@objectstack/plugin-auth` `patch` with `Metadata-protocol: none`. Right under ruling A on #25105 and the AGENTS.md changeset rule: no authorable key, accepted value, metadata type, default or meaning changes (the `internal` declaration on `sys_verification.identifier` is untouched), so the kind is `none` and a non-protocol services fix ships `patch`. The `Check Changeset` run on this head is green, and the two declaration lines agree in value and kind across the PR body and the changeset.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **`sys-verification.object.ts:113-116` still says `identifier` has no readback row "because no better-auth flow reads it back off a row"** (PR Acceptance notes; dev report out-of-scope finding 1, carrier none). Confirmed stale at `origin/main`, and now plainly contradicted by the seam table. It is a comment with no behaviour behind it, it sits in `packages/platform-objects/**`, which the dispatch fenced off for `domain:engine`, and the remedy did not need the declaration changed, so leaving it out of this diff was the right call. Not blocking. Escalated to the dispatching seat: a follow-up card to `domain:engine` to restamp that sentence so the next reader is not told the census is empty.

2. **`findMany` and `consumeOne` pass no lookup to the seam, so `identifier` costs one id-batched privileged read per verification `findMany` / `consumeOne`** (Acceptance notes; dev report finding 2). Confirmed at `objectql-adapter.ts:1010` and `:1154`; `findOne` (:955) passes its `where`. `findVerificationValue` is a `findMany` keyed on `identifier` with limit 1 (internal-adapter.mjs:752-765), so each verification lookup now issues two privileged id-batched reads instead of one; `consumeVerificationValue` adds a `findMany` then a `consumeOne` keyed on `id`, where a lookup could not answer `identifier` anyway. One-time flows, correctness unaffected, and the file is outside the dispatched surface. Not blocking. Answered: a performance follow-up that passes `findMany`'s `where` as the seam's lookup is reasonable and separate.

3. **The new suite's module import is about 18 s on the shared dev box** (Acceptance notes). Same shape as the sibling real-engine suite `internal-credential-readback.test.ts`; the Test Core shards that run it are still in progress on this head. Answered: not a contract matter; the shard conclusions say whether the wall is acceptable.

4. **The merge commit `731668228` carries git's default message without the trailer pair** (dev report deviation 1). The reviewed object is the net diff against `main`, which is unaffected, and the authored commits carry the trailers. Answered: not blocking.

5. **The gate runner's PID was found with `pgrep -f`, verified via `/proc` before `tail --pid`, and nothing was killed** (dev report deviation 2). Process hygiene inside the dev's own run; no repository state was touched. Answered: not blocking.

6. **The dispatch's Clause-② expectation** asked the dev to re-declare from the diff if the remedy changed which records are accepted beyond the instructed one. The dev kept `no` and stated the whole delta in a table; by ② that reading is right, and no re-declaration is owed.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-25111-sso-dns-record`
Reviewed-by: `session_01UnHcTADjeg3VwxF21QHj7W`

**VERDICT: PASS**
